# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 12 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

None yet.

You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.

- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.

- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.

- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.

- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.

You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 12 turns.

- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.

- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.

You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 12 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

saw.prompt:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 12 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.

saw.prompt:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 12 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.

You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 12 turns.

- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.

Pirate-1 final report:

I spent all 12 turns and never entered the cave. My path was:
- Dug A6, B6, C6, D6.
- Moved east along row 6: B6, C6, D6, E6.
- Read the scroll three times; it was empty every time.

From my perspective, the main problem was coordination. I never saw a single message from pirates 2–4; the scroll stayed empty. That meant if anyone found the cave, I had no way to know in time, and after turn 8 or so I had too few turns left to travel anywhere useful.

Design notes:
- The scoring strongly rewards finding the cave early and immediately telling everyone where it is. A pre-agreed protocol like “if you find the cave, write `CAVE <square>` on the scroll” would help, but reading the scroll also costs a turn, so pirates must balance searching with checking.
- Maybe the initial setup should give a recommended search division, since the scroll starts empty and there is no way to coordinate before the first turns are spent.
- I was physically constrained by pirate-2 being directly south of me all game, which limited my movement to the top row only.
- A better plan for me would have been to leave more turns for reading and travelling, not to sweep an entire row without checking whether the cave had already been found.

I’m Pirate-2, and my game has just ended. Here is my final reflection on what happened and what I think the crew could have done better.

---

## What I did

My actions in order:

1. `dig A5` — no cave
2. `move east to B5`
3. `dig B5` — no cave
4. `move east to C5`
5. `dig C5` — no cave
6. `read` — scroll was empty
7. `move east to D5`
8. `dig D5` — no cave
9. `read` — scroll was empty
10. `move east to E5`
11. `dig E5` — no cave
12. `read` — scroll was empty

So I searched five squares in row 5 (A5–E5), found nothing, and never learned that the cave had been found (if it was). I never entered the cave.

---

## What I inferred about the game state

From the very first turns, it looked like the pirates started in a vertical column along the west edge:

- Pirate-1 at A6
- Pirate-2 (me) at A5
- Pirate-3 at A4
- Pirate-4 probably at A3

I assumed the intended pattern was that each pirate would sweep east along their starting row: P1 along row 6, me along row 5, P3 along row 4, P4 along row 3. The blockers I saw supported this: Pirate-1 stayed north of me, Pirate-3 south of me, and my east moves were clean. That is why I kept moving east and digging along row 5.

I also paused twice to read the scroll, hoping someone had found the cave and written its location. Each time it was empty.

---

## What went wrong / main risks

1. **Too much searching, too little coordination.**  
   A row sweep covers rows 3–6 but never searches rows 1–2. The cave could have been in an unsearched row the whole time.

2. **No scroll protocol.**  
   Nobody wrote anything to the scroll. If someone did find the cave, they did not communicate it—or if they wrote it, by the time I read, it still didn't appear. We had no agreed system like: *“If you find it, immediately write ‘CAVE at X’.”*

3. **Reading costs turns.**  
   I spent three turns reading and learned nothing. But reading is necessary only if someone actually writes. A better plan would set a fixed reading schedule, or have one pirate act as the main reader.

4. **I ended with a low-value final turn.**  
   By turn 12 I was at E5, with F5 still undug, but I could not both move to F5 and dig it in one turn. So my last turn could only be a read or a pointless move. In the future, a pirate should stop searching earlier to preserve turns for traveling/entering once the cave is known.

---

## What I think the crew should do next time

- **Divide the island into clear zones.** For example:
  - P1: row 6
  - P2: row 5
  - P3: row 4
  - P4: rows 1–3 (sweeping south/east or using a different route)
  This avoids leaving the bottom two rows completely unsearched.

- **Set an explicit rule: the first pirate to find the cave writes it immediately.** For example, one line: `CAVE at B4`. Without that, the finder’s knowledge dies with them if they enter.

- **Set a reading rhythm.** Maybe every 3rd turn, each pirate reads the scroll. That way a cave announcement is picked up quickly.

- **Reserve entry turns.** A pirate should not use their last turn digging a square unless they can afford to write + enter afterward. For example, when I had 3 turns left at D5, it might have been better to go toward a likely central area and wait to be told where the cave was, rather than blindly sweeping further.

- **Use the scroll for searched squares too**, or at least row-completion updates like `P2 searched A5-E5`, to prevent double digging and to make clear which regions are still open.

---
